bremen-far.name: Bremen

sights.name: Rathaus
sights.content: This is one of the finest in Europe and has been included on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Building work started in 1410 and it is seen as an important display of the wealth and freedom of the city.

sights.name: Roland
sights.content: This statue on the main square, in front of the town hall, is of the Knight Roland, subject of the Medieval epic, the Song of Roland, who was a protector of trade. He appears in many European cities, especially those involved in the Hanseat

sights.name: Dom St. Petri
sights.hours: Mon–Fri 10:00–17:00, Sat 10:00–14:00, Sun 14:00–17:00 (Check website for tower hours)
sights.price: Free entry to cathedral; Tower and Museum: €3–5
sights.content: Over 1,200 years old, its huge towered façade dominates the main square. The interior is also impressive, with some fine painted details on the ceilings. The cathedral was damaged by fire and lightning in the 17th century and also seriously

sights.name: Böttcherstraße
sights.content: An incredible ''Jugendstil'' (Art Nouveau) street that runs from the main square towards the river. There are many fine façades and courtyards all with large amounts of design detail. There is an impressive Glockenspiel that chimes at regul

sights.name: Wallanlagen
sights.content: Built on the site of the former city fortifications, this star-shaped park is the oldest public garden in Germany. It features scenic walking paths, colorful flowerbeds, and the historic "Am Wall" windmill.

sights.name: Schnoor
sights.content: Bremen's oldest district, characterized by narrow lanes and timber-framed houses dating back to the 15th and 16th centuries. Once a quarter for fishermen and craftsmen, it now hosts numerous galleries, cafés, and small handicraft shops.

sights.name: Focke Museum
sights.price: permanent exhibition €6, children €2, and special exhibition €8, children €4
sights.content: A good overview of the history of Bremen City with a wide range of collections.

sights.name: Universum Science Center
sights.content: Science museum with plenty of interactive exhibits such as an earthquake simulator. The main building is a huge steel shell designed by the Bremen architect Thomas Klumpp.

sights.name: Hafenmuseum Speicher XI
sights.content: Housed in a former cotton warehouse. Models of ships used during the past.

sights.name: Gerhard-Marcks-Haus
sights.content: The contemporary art museum shows the work of [[w:Gerhard Marcks

sights.name: Wilhelm-Wagenfeld-Haus
sights.content: Founded as a design museum but also used for exhibitions in modern art. The museum is named after [[w:Wilhelm Wagenfeld

sights.name: Weserburg
sights.content: Modern art museum located on the Teerhof peninsula.

sights.name: St. Marien
sights.hours: Mon-Sat 10:00-17:00 Sun 13:00-17:00; The church will be closed for renovation work from 2 November 2026 until expected May 2027
sights.content: The largest church in Lübeck, and a key example of brick Gothic architecture. Built between 1277 and 1351, it features the highest brick vault in the world.

sights.name: The Dom
sights.content: Founded in 1173 by Henry the Lion, this is one of the oldest monuments in Lübeck and the first large brick church built on the Baltic coast. Initially constructed as a Romanesque basilica and later converted into a Gothic hall church, it is

sights.name: St. Petri
sights.content: Its tower platform (which can be reached by an elevator) offers a great view over the city, and if weather conditions allow it you can even see Travemünde (17 km to the north-east).

sights.name: St. Jakobi
sights.content: This 14th-century seafarers' church survived World War II intact, preserving its original historic interior. It is known for its historic pipe organs and a memorial chapel dedicated to the lost sailing ship ''Pamir''.

sights.name: St. Aegidien
sights.content: The smallest of Lübeck's five medieval parish churches was spared from destruction in World War II. Its interior combines medieval frescoes with a carved 1587 Renaissance singers' gallery and a prominent Baroque altar.

sights.name: St. Katharinen
sights.content: This early 14th-century former Franciscan monastery church is the only surviving conventual church in Lübeck's Old Town. Today operating as a museum, it features an elevated choir built over a double-nave crypt and exterior sculptures by Er

sights.name: Holstentor
sights.content: Being featured on the pre-reunification 50-mark banknote, this gate is easily the most recognised landmark of Lübeck in Germany. The gate nowadays hosts a museum.

sights.name: Behnhaus/Drägerhaus
sights.content: A Classicist burgher house that now hosts an art museum.

sights.name: Rathaus
sights.content: Its architecture is a stylistic potpourri reaching back to the 12th century. It is still the seat of the city administration and not a museum, so you can't have a look inside on your own. But there are guided tours every hour or so where th

sights.name: Willy Brandt House
sights.content: Dedicated to the former chancellor (1969-1974) and leader of the Social Democratic Party who was born in Lübeck in 1912.

sights.name: Haus der Kaufmannschaft
sights.content: A building built by the wealthy merchants.

sights.name: Buddenbrookhaus
sights.content: Dedicated to the brothers Thomas and Heinrich Mann, who spent their youth there. It contains many of their works. Closed until 2023.

sights.name: Günter-Grass-Haus
sights.content: Dedicated to the author (born in Gdańsk) who spent most of his life in Lübeck until his death in 2015 and who received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1999.

sights.name: Museumshafen
sights.content: It features some old-fashioned ships, among them a rebuilt Hanseatic ''kraweel'' ("Lisa von Lübeck") — more so in winter, because many of these ships are still in use during summer.

sights.name: European Hansemuseum
sights.price: €16 for adults in main exhibition, reduced price €10, free for children (under 18), university students
sights.content: Opened in 2015, this is perhaps the "crown jewel" among Lübeck's historical museums as it gives an in-depth look into Lübeck's over 800 years of history and how Lübeck shaped the Hanseatic League and how the ''Hanse'' in turn shaped Lübeck.

sights.name: Industriemuseum Geschichtswerkstatt Herrenwyk
sights.content: Dedicated to the [[Industrial tourism

sights.content: As Lübeck's eastern border was co-extensive with the border between West (FRG) and East Germany (GDR) during the [[Cold War Europe

sights.name: Theaterfigurenmuseum Lübeck
sights.content: A museum dedicated to all kinds of theatre puppets.

sights.name: Museum für Natur und Umwelt Lübeck
sights.content: A natural history museum featuring, among other things, an entire sperm whale skeleton taken from an unlucky whale that died in a beaching incident.
